title: Client partnership quarterly deck roadmap + commitment ledger
content:
Purpose:
A compact, facilitator-focused QBR deck template for customer success managers that covers both Standard and Enterprise rhythms. The goal is rapid prep (30–60m) + consistent renewal-oriented outcomes: adoption, risk reduction, opportunity identification, and a signed next-step commitment ledger.

Audience:
- Primary: CSMs + AMs preparing executive + technical QBRs
- Secondary: Solutions engineers, renewal specialists, customer execs

How to use this doc:
- Copy the slide order below into a fresh deck. For Standard customers, use the trimmed variant (marked STANDARD). For Enterprise customers, use the EXPANDED sections and add the technical appendix.
- Use the Renewal Ledger (CSV sample) to record agreed next steps live during the meeting.

Suggested slide order (STANDARD) -- 8–10 slides, 20–30m:
1. Cover + meeting outcomes (1 slide) -- objective, timebox, attendees
2. Where we started (1 slide) -- contract summary, baseline metrics (ARR, seats, token usage)
3. What we delivered / recent wins (1 slide) -- highlights, adoption stories, quoted metrics
4. Health snapshot (1 slide) -- usage trend sparkline, latency/availability flags, NPS trend
5. Risk & blockers (1 slide) -- top 3 risks, owner, mitigation next steps
6. Opportunities / roadmap alignment (1 slide) -- product fit, upsell signals, pilot ideas
7. Renewal timeline & ask (1 slide) -- renewal window, target outcome, ask options
8. Commitment ledger + action items (1 slide) -- live-fill commitments

Suggested slide order (ENTERPRISE) -- 12–18 slides, 45–60m:
1. Cover + tailored outcomes (1 slide)
2. Exec summary: health + renewal posture (1 slide)
3. Contract & entitlements deep-dive (1 slide)
4. Adoption cohorts & ROI narrative (1–2 slides) -- user segments, business KPIs tied to usage
5. Performance & SLOs (1 slide) -- external latency, error rates, incident summary past quarter
6. Security & compliance items (1 slide) -- audit requests, controls status
7. Integration & roadmap alignment (1 slide) -- product gaps, joint roadmap ask matrix
8. Risk matrix + mitigation timeline (1 slide) -- owners, severity, ETA on fixes
9. Commercials & renewal levers (1 slide) -- pricing options, term suggestions, incentives
10. Executive asks & decision calendar (1 slide)
11. Commitment ledger (live) + signatures (1 slide)
12. Appendix: technical runbook, logs, eval summary (multiple)

Renewal ledger (live tracker) -- CSV header suggestion:
customer_id,customer_name,cs_owner,renewal_target_date,current_term_end,thresholds_for_renewal,agreed_next_step,decision_owner,decision_date,probability,notes

Playbook: pre-meeting checklist (CSM):
- Confirm attendees and decision-maker presence (Slack confirm 2 days prior)
- Pull usage by cohort (last 90d), list top 5 endpoint latency percentiles, open incidents this quarter
- Run readiness check: contract terms, outstanding POs, billing flags
- Draft 2–3 renewal offers tailored to customer usage and risk
- Share pre-read 72h before meeting (1 page)

Playbook: facilitation script (key snippets):
- Opening (2–3m): restate outcomes "Today we want to align on value delivered, any blockers, and agree a renewal path by X date."
- Health review (5–8m): show usage + one case study. Ask: "What surprised you in these numbers?" Pause for 30s.
- Risk surfacing (5m): present top risks, ask for root causes and required support. Assign owner and ETA.
- Ask & close (5–10m): present renewal options, recommend a path, capture verbal signal and fill the Commitment Ledger in real time.

Risk scoring rubric (quick):
- Green: low/no blocker, usage stable/growing, exec engaged
- Amber: moderate adoption gaps OR 1 unresolved technical blocker, renewal probability 50–75%
- Red: key outcome unmet, exec churn signals, unresolved billing/compliance, probability <50%

Standard vs Enterprise tilt notes:
- STANDARD: focus on adoption narrative + simple commercial ask. Keep technical appendix optional.
- ENTERPRISE: expect more legal/commercial questions; include SLO history, compliance matrix, and a dedicated technical appendix with incident logs and mitigation plan.

Sample follow-up email template (post-meeting):
Subject: Next steps from our QBR on [date] -- [Customer name]
Body: Thanks for your time. Attached: slide deck + commitment ledger snapshot. Summary: 3 bullets (health, risk, ask). Comms: Decision owner: [name] by [date]. Action items: 1) [owner] - [task] - due [date].

Common slips & reminders:
- Don’t overstuff the deck; use the appendix for detail.
- Always capture the verbal commitment live and convert to written follow-up within 24h.
- For Enterprise accounts, get procurement and security on the calendar before final pricing discussion.

Open questions / TODOs for the template itself:
- Add a slide module for "cost per successful inference" (need input from ML infra on tokens -> $) -- action: Benji to pull sample rates (JIRA-CS-4180).
- Determine a concise one-page pre-read layout for enterprise execs -- action: Rina to draft v1 by 2024-02-02.

Notes to self / scratchpad (choppy):
- consider adding quick export from renewal tracker -> calendar invites
- keep the Commitment Ledger CSV under drive template folder so CSMs can import
- maybe include a one-slide runbook for incident response for SRE ops for enterprise meetings

Appendix ideas (placeholders):
- One-slide ROI case: baseline metric, delta, projected 12-month impact
- One-slide Incident timeline (if >1 P1 in quarter)

End of draft.

(Author: Ayesha Patel -- CSM enablement; last edited 2024-02-12)
